section_summary: This section documents State and War Department administration of travel to occupied Japan, including military permits, passport validation, alien transit by commercial aircraft, business-traveler quotas, missionaries, and individual entry cases. It also contains SCAP directives governing quarantine ports and missionary support, applications from traders, and correspondence about admitting foreign commercial and religious personnel. By late November 1947, the military authorities ended documentation requirements for ordinary airline passengers transiting Japan and placed responsibility on the carriers.

subfiles.title: Telegram querying SCAP on Shanghai transit request
subfiles.about: Reports that SCAP is being queried concerning the consul's July 17 telegram.
subfiles.summary: The Department tells Shanghai that SCAP is being consulted.

subfiles.title: Incoming telegram concerning alien transit documentation
subfiles.about: Requests guidance on documentation required for non-American passengers transiting Japan.
subfiles.summary: A largely garbled telegram asks whether non-American transit passengers require passport validation or military documentation.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on consular authority to validate alien passports
subfiles.from: Edward Williams III, Division of Protective Services
subfiles.about: Records discussion with the War Department over whether existing authority covered alien air passengers.
subfiles.summary: Williams and Flickinger concluded that the CINCFE authorization clearly covered Americans but not aliens; the Military Permit Section would ask Tokyo for clarification.

subfiles.title: Authorization for Manila to validate transit passports
subfiles.about: Authorizes passport validation for air passengers making only refueling or emergency stops in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Manila may validate passports for direct air transit, with passengers and carriers responsible for conduct during stops in Japan.

subfiles.title: Circular authorizing validation of American passports for Japan transit
subfiles.to: Selected American diplomatic and consular posts
subfiles.about: Delegates authority to endorse American passports for minimal-stop air transit through Japan.
subfiles.summary: Posts at Nanking, Shanghai, Peiping, Hong Kong, Seoul, Manila, and Vancouver receive a prescribed endorsement for American citizens transiting Japan by air.

subfiles.title: CINCFE proposal to delegate Japan transit clearances
subfiles.to: War Department for the Joint Chiefs of Staff
subfiles.about: Proposes delegating authority to consular and State representatives to clear American air passengers transiting Japan.
subfiles.summary: CINCFE argues that local passport validation would reduce delays, correspondence, and radio traffic. Clearances would permit only refueling or emergency stops, with travelers subject to SCAP control and carriers morally responsible for them.

subfiles.title: Shanghai record-copy filing sheet
subfiles.about: Controls the return and filing of a Shanghai record copy.
subfiles.summary: Record-copy sheet directing that the Shanghai copy be returned for central filing.

subfiles.title: Request for Hulda Zarnack to enter Japan
subfiles.about: Seeks permission for German YWCA official Hulda Zarnack to attend a Japanese YWCA gathering.
subfiles.summary: Zarnack planned to fly to Japan in early November with an international YWCA delegation, but her Berlin travel document was not valid for Japan.

subfiles.title: Circular extending air-transit procedure to aliens
subfiles.to: Selected American diplomatic and consular posts
subfiles.about: Extends the July 3 Japan air-transit passport-validation procedure from American citizens to aliens.
subfiles.summary: The Department informs posts in East Asia and Vancouver that the existing commercial-aircraft transit procedure now applies to aliens.

subfiles.title: Inquiry to Berlin concerning Hulda Zarnack
subfiles.about: Asks whether the Combined Travel Board favors validating Zarnack's document for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Before consulting Tokyo, the Department asks Berlin to assess Zarnack's proposed YWCA visit and notes doubts about its relevance to occupation programs.

subfiles.title: Philippine Embassy acknowledgment concerning four officials
subfiles.about: Reports that four Philippine officials had already sailed before Japan-visit requirements could be conveyed.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy thanks the Department but explains that Roxas, Salcedo, Brillantes, and Guerzon departed San Francisco on September 19.

subfiles.title: Transmission of David Kumetz travel approval and permit
subfiles.about: Forwards Commerce approval and a military permit for alien businessman David Kumetz.
subfiles.summary: Shipley forwards Kumetz's Commerce approval and Japan military permit for action.

subfiles.title: David Kumetz application to visit Japan
subfiles.to: Departments of Commerce and State and SCAP
subfiles.about: Applies to visit Japanese cities to buy and sell general merchandise for United States and Mexican trade.
subfiles.summary: Kumetz, an importer-exporter with prewar Japan experience, proposes purchasing Japanese goods for the United States and Mexico and selling imports in Japan.

subfiles.title: Kumetz company letter supporting Japan application
subfiles.from: S. Y. Allen, Kumetz Export and Import Company
subfiles.to: Department of Commerce, Office of International Trade
subfiles.about: Supports David Kumetz's application and explains his Mexican citizenship and role in the corporation.
subfiles.summary: The company states that Kumetz is its president, a Mexican citizen seeking United States naturalization, and its most suitable international-trade agent.

subfiles.title: Closure of Bertie Deveson entry case
subfiles.about: Records that Deveson received his military permit and arranged an exit-permit waiver.
subfiles.summary: Deveson's Japan travel case was closed after both requirements were resolved.

subfiles.title: INS letter on Bertie Deveson's reentry permit
subfiles.from: Joseph Savoretti, Immigration and Naturalization Service
subfiles.about: Explains that a reentry permit depends on obtaining a State Department departure permit.
subfiles.summary: INS holds Deveson's reentry application pending State Department action on his alien departure permit.

subfiles.title: Bertie Deveson's alien departure application
subfiles.about: Applies for permission to leave the United States for a six-month business trip to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Deveson, a British merchant and W. T. Grant Company representative, records residence in Yokohama and Washington, family and passport details, and plans to depart through San Francisco. He intends to return after about six months and has applied for a reentry permit.

subfiles.title: Charge slip for New Delhi telegram
subfiles.about: Records the temporary charge of a telegram associated with New Delhi.
subfiles.summary: Charge slip for a New Delhi telegram in the Japan travel file.

subfiles.title: Conversation concerning Husni Halabi's application
subfiles.about: Requests the standard Japan-entry application from the Lebanese Legation for Husni Halabi.
subfiles.summary: Mattar agreed to submit Halabi's missing application and accepted the conversation as acknowledgment of the Legation's note.

subfiles.title: Notification of M. A. Samman's Japan clearance
subfiles.about: Informs the Syrian Legation that Samman was cleared under the Japanese traders quota.
subfiles.summary: Samman could enter during October 1–21 for a 21-day stay; the Legation would document him under SCAP Circular 8.

subfiles.title: Military permit for Japan traders-quota travel
subfiles.about: Authorizes entry into Japan under the traders quota for 21 days after arrival.
subfiles.summary: Military permit number 47-13169 authorizes traders-quota travel to Japan.

subfiles.title: Swiss Legation memorandum concerning Alice Kaelin
subfiles.about: Reports that the prescribed statement was attached to Alice Kaelin's passport in lieu of a military permit.
subfiles.summary: The Swiss Legation documented Kaelin under paragraph 7b of SCAP Circular 8.

subfiles.title: Submission of Husni Halabi's application to the Army
subfiles.about: Forwards Halabi's application for consideration under the business quota assigned to other nations.
subfiles.summary: The Military Permit Section is asked to submit Halabi's business application to SCAP.

subfiles.title: Clearance of James Keen and Palamadai S. Lokanathan
subfiles.from: G. P. Lynch, Military Permit Section
subfiles.about: States there is no military objection to Keen and Lokanathan traveling to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Theater headquarters had already notified Keen in Shanghai of both travelers' clearance.

subfiles.title: Airgram concerning three missionaries in Brazil
subfiles.about: Authorizes transit-visa processing for three missionaries cleared to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: Yoshida, Kircher, and Gemeinder may receive transit visas and must contact Protective Services in the United States for permits and exit arrangements.

subfiles.title: Airgram concerning two missionaries in Rome
subfiles.about: Authorizes transit-visa processing for Johannes Ponzelet and Josef H. Thoneick.
subfiles.summary: The two German missionaries were cleared for Japan and were to arrange military and exit permits while transiting the United States.

subfiles.title: Despatch transmitting Japan quarantine directive
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits SCAP's directive designating Japanese ports of entry and requiring quarantine services.
subfiles.summary: Cover despatch for SCAPIN 1787 on ports and quarantine facilities.

subfiles.title: SCAP directive designating quarantine ports
subfiles.about: Designates twelve Japanese ports of entry and orders quarantine services at them.
subfiles.summary: SCAP names Otaru, Hakodate, Yokohama, Yokosuka, Shimizu, Nagoya, Kobe, Kure, Moji, Sasebo, Nagasaki, and Miike as entry ports.

subfiles.title: SCAP information memorandum on quarantine procedures
subfiles.about: Explains the background and surveillance requirements accompanying SCAPIN 1787.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum cites prior entry and quarantine regulations and calls for routine surveillance.

subfiles.title: Letter transmitting Maji Meesa Ismail's file
subfiles.about: Sends Ismail's personal file in response to a Senate office request.
subfiles.summary: Robinson forwards Ismail's file concerning proposed business travel to Japan.

subfiles.title: Despatch transmitting missionary-aid directive
subfiles.about: Transmits an Eighth Army directive explaining admission and support rules for missionaries.
subfiles.summary: Cover despatch for Operational Directive 65 on military assistance to missionaries in Japan.

subfiles.title: Operational Directive 65: Extension of Aid to Missionaries
subfiles.about: Restates SCAP policy for admitting, supplying, housing, and assisting missionaries in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Missionaries require financial, housing, and professional assurances; representative missionaries may receive temporary revenue-basis support, while operating missionaries receive only limited emergency aid. The directive regulates dependents, shipments, postal privileges, transport, military facilities, vehicles, and exceptional visits by senior church officials.

subfiles.title: Airgram concerning Sister Anna Tellen
subfiles.about: Authorizes local documentation of Sister Anna Tellen for missionary travel to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Tellen could receive revenue-basis surface transport and an English clearance statement in lieu of a military permit.

subfiles.title: Airgram concerning Josef Kumezo Kakihori
subfiles.about: Authorizes transit-visa processing for a Japanese missionary residing in Argentina.
subfiles.summary: Kakihori was cleared for Japan and instructed to obtain his permit and exit arrangements while passing through the United States.

subfiles.title: Airgram concerning Antoine De Changy
subfiles.about: Authorizes documentation and surface transportation for Father De Changy's missionary travel to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The French Consulate could issue De Changy a SCAP-compliant English clearance statement serving in lieu of a military permit.

subfiles.title: Army request for Faez Abdallah Ejel's travel details
subfiles.from: G. P. Lynch, Military Permit Section
subfiles.about: Requests information about the ship on which Ejel would proceed to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The theater required Ejel's intended vessel before completing travel arrangements.

subfiles.title: Conversation resolving inquiry about Faez Abdallah Ejel
subfiles.about: Explains that Ejel had already begun traveling to Japan via London and Bombay.
subfiles.summary: Captain Keough agreed to review the file, and the latest request could be ignored unless he responded further.

subfiles.title: File note concerning Siamese applicants
subfiles.about: Notes that the Siamese men in Lynch's letter were handled separately.
subfiles.summary: The Siamese applicants mentioned by Lynch belonged to a separate case.

subfiles.title: File note concerning Meyer Abadi
subfiles.about: Notes that Meyer Abadi was handled as a separate case.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference separating Abadi's case from Lynch's other applicants.

subfiles.title: SCAP rejection of incomplete trader applications
subfiles.about: Requests fuller information for Meyer Abadi and six Siamese business applicants.
subfiles.summary: SCAP would reconsider applications providing detailed business purposes, routes, transportation, and a specified 15-day arrival window. Siam's quota was two, and applicants were limited to private traders or service representatives staying 21 days.

subfiles.title: Recommendation to notify Panama of Abadi's rejection
subfiles.about: Recommends signing a note explaining why SCAP rejected Meyer Abadi's application.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum proposes inviting Abadi to submit a more detailed application.

subfiles.title: Draft note to Panama concerning Meyer Abadi
subfiles.to: Eugenio J. Chevalier, Panamanian chargé d'affaires ad interim
subfiles.about: Explains the deficiencies in Abadi's application and the conditions for resubmission.
subfiles.summary: SCAP requires the goods or services involved, route and means of travel, and a specific 15-day entry period. Any permit would allow a 21-day stay, subject to possible short extension, and the Department offers to forward a revised application.

subfiles.title: Commerce request to cancel David Kumetz's October travel
subfiles.from: Office of International Trade, Areas Branch
subfiles.about: Requests cancellation of Kumetz's permit if it had not already been forwarded.
subfiles.summary: Commerce reports that Kumetz was no longer interested in near-term Japan travel.

subfiles.title: Los Angeles report on David Kumetz's withdrawals
subfiles.from: Walter Measday, Los Angeles Regional Office
subfiles.about: Reports that Kumetz declined both September and October opportunities to travel to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Kumetz first cited a Jewish holiday, then inconvenience, leaving the regional office doubtful about his immediate plans.

subfiles.title: Commerce memorandum requesting Kumetz cancellation
subfiles.about: Forwards the regional report and asks that Kumetz's October permit be canceled.
subfiles.summary: Commerce asks State to cancel Kumetz's unused permit.

subfiles.title: Return of David Kumetz's military permit
subfiles.about: Returns Kumetz's unused permit because he could not travel under the existing clearance.
subfiles.summary: The Army is asked to cancel Kumetz's permit; future travel would require a new application.

subfiles.title: Delivery of Japan permit to Mr. Katzman
subfiles.about: Sends a military permit and confirms waiver of the alien exit-permit requirement.
subfiles.summary: Katzman could enter Japan October 19–30 for 21 days; immigration offices were notified of his exit-permit waiver.

subfiles.title: Army inquiry about alien air-transit authorization
subfiles.about: Asks whether selected consuls and domestic officials may authorize foreign nationals to transit Japan by air.
subfiles.summary: Lynch seeks confirmation before instructing airlines, noting reports of passengers traveling without military transit permits.

subfiles.title: Circular applying Japan transit procedure to aliens
subfiles.to: Selected American diplomatic and consular posts
subfiles.about: Makes the July 3 commercial-aircraft transit authorization applicable to aliens.
subfiles.summary: The Department extends the existing procedure to foreign nationals at designated Asian and Canadian posts.

subfiles.title: State Department objections to authorizing alien transit
subfiles.about: Questions whether State and its posts should assume responsibility for authorizing foreign nationals to transit Japan.
subfiles.summary: Chappell argues that aliens' governments and SCAP should decide their eligibility because State lacks both jurisdiction and screening information. He suggests carrier responsibility or strictly pro forma documentation and considers rescinding the October 22 consular authorization.

subfiles.title: Termination of transit-documentation requirement
subfiles.about: Announces that civilian airline passengers no longer need documents merely to transit Japan.
subfiles.summary: Airlines must warn passengers about SCAP rules and accept responsibility for their conduct during stops.

subfiles.title: Berlin support for Hulda Zarnack's entry
subfiles.about: Reports occupation and Combined Travel Board support for Zarnack's proposed YWCA visit.
subfiles.summary: OMGUS considered Zarnack capable of interpreting Japanese democratic progress to German women and youth; the Combined Travel Board had no objection to validation.

subfiles.title: Instructions to Shanghai concerning Hulda Zarnack
subfiles.about: Permits validation of Zarnack's document if SCAP grants entry.
subfiles.summary: Shanghai should seek SCAP's decision directly or through Tokyo, with Berlin's favorable assessment supplied for context.

subfiles.title: Notification to SCAP concerning Hulda Zarnack
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Relays Berlin's favorable assessment of Zarnack and notes that Shanghai was instructed to request entry permission.
subfiles.summary: SCAP receives OMGUS, USPOLAD, and Combined Travel Board views supporting Zarnack's YWCA visit.

subfiles.title: ITT request for permanent American personnel in Japan
subfiles.about: Requests permission to station technical, legal, accounting, and manufacturing personnel at two Japanese subsidiaries.
subfiles.summary: Fullam argues that American managers could improve communications-equipment production, protect and recover ITT property, and assist occupation authorities. He proposes Clinton B. Allsopp, George J. Eder, C. A. Hayne, S. H. Larrabee, F. E. Samuels, A. C. Chisholm, and R. C. Keefer for specified posts.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Goldman and Yanowitch approvals
subfiles.about: Forwards Commerce certificates approving two alien businessmen for the November Japan-traders quota.
subfiles.summary: Commerce approvals are attached for Alfred Goldman and Isaak Yanowitch.

subfiles.title: Alfred Goldman application to visit Japan
subfiles.to: Departments of Commerce and State and SCAP
subfiles.about: Applies to visit Kobe, Yokohama, and Nagoya for import-export business.
subfiles.summary: Goldman identifies his New York agency, export product lines, and former Japanese offices, referring to an attached letter for his prewar history and detailed purpose.

subfiles.title: Alfred Goldman statement supporting Japan travel
subfiles.about: Explains Goldman's long Japanese business experience and plans to reopen offices and settle wartime claims.
subfiles.summary: Goldman managed J. Witkowski & Company in Japan, handling substantial international imports and exports before the war. He seeks to investigate confiscated stock, settle banking obligations, restore worldwide trade, and reopen Japanese offices linked to his New York business.

subfiles.title: Speedletter concerning Alfred Goldman's permit
subfiles.about: Notifies Goldman of his Japan clearance and requests information needed to deliver the permit.
subfiles.summary: Goldman could enter November 16–30 for 21 days and was asked to visit Washington or provide passport and departure details.

subfiles.title: Speedletter concerning Isaak Yanowitch's permit
subfiles.about: Notifies Yanowitch of his Japan clearance and requests information needed to deliver the permit.
subfiles.summary: Yanowitch could enter December 16–30 for 21 days and was asked to visit Washington or provide passport and departure details.
